content:
The test image shows a mango leaf with discrete, dark brown/black necrotic spots scattered across the leaf surface. The spots are roughly circular, well-defined, and some appear to have a darker center. The rest of the leaf is green and healthy-looking. This pattern suggests a fungal disease causing localized lesions.

Key features:
- Discrete dark necrotic lesions (not a coating or film)
- Multiple spots distributed across the leaf
- Some lesions appear sunken or with shot-hole appearance
- Green background tissue otherwise healthy

This looks most consistent with **Anthracnose** (dark, discrete lesions) rather than Powdery Mildew (white powder), Sooty Mould (black sooty coating), or Die Back (tip/margin dieback).

Let me view one Anthracnose reference to confirm.

The Anthracnose reference shows a more advanced/yellowed leaf stage, but I've used my budget.

Comparing the test image to all class descriptions:
- **Anthracnose**: dark, discrete necrotic spots/lesions on leaves — matches the test image (multiple dark circular lesions on a green leaf)
- **Die_Back**: dieback from tips/margins — doesn't match (no tip necrosis, spots are mid-leaf)
- **Powdery_Mildew**: white powdery coating — doesn't match (lesions are dark, not white powder)
- **Sooty_Mould**: black sooty surface coating — doesn't match (lesions are discrete spots, not a coating)

The discrete dark necrotic circular spots on an otherwise green leaf are the hallmark presentation of Anthracnose on mango.
